summary: Code review of useMatchmakingQueue hook and HomeScreen Quick Play additions. No critical issues found. The state machine is correct, cleanup is thorough, and the implementation follows existing patterns. Two warnings: (1) missing double-tap guard on join() unlike the adjacent startChallenge, (2) missing focus-visible styles on ModeCard and overlay buttons. Three informational notes on reduced-motion, empty matched-state overlay frame, and duplicated category slug constant.
goal: Review 1v1 Quick Play implementation for correctness, conventions, race conditions, resource leaks, and accessibility

findings.issue: No double-tap guard on join(). Unlike startChallenge which checks `if (challengeBusy) return`, join() can be called multiple times before React re-renders to show the overlay. A rapid double-tap fires two POSTs, wasting a rate limit token (30/hour budget). The server handles the second call gracefully (409) and startPolling is idempotent, so no resource leak or state corruption — just unnecessary rate limit consumption.
findings.fix: Add an early return when status is not idle: `if (state.status !== 'idle' && state.status !== 'timeout' && state.status !== 'error') return;` at the top of join(), or use a ref-based busy guard like challengeBusy.

findings.issue: Missing focus-visible styles on ModeCard button and all SearchingOverlay buttons (Cancel, Search again, Try again, Back). The mobile CSS has no global button:focus-visible rule. Other mobile buttons (Play hero at line 145, ProfileScreen toggles, BottomNav) consistently include explicit focus-visible:ring-* classes. This violates the project's WCAG 2.1 AA standard per context/ux-accessibility.md.
findings.fix: Add `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-signal focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-void` to the ModeCard button className and each SearchingOverlay button className.

findings.issue: The spinner uses bare animate-spin without motion-reduce:animate-none. The web Spinner.tsx component includes this guard, but existing mobile spinners (DuelRoomScreen) also omit it. Consistent with mobile patterns but violates DESIGN.md's stated 'all motion is prefers-reduced-motion guarded' rule.
findings.fix: Add `motion-reduce:animate-none` to the spinner className. Consider a shared mobile Spinner component.

findings.issue: The 'matched' status renders an empty overlay for one React frame before the navigation effect fires, since queueActive includes all non-idle statuses but SearchingOverlay has no visual handler for 'matched'.
findings.fix: Either exclude 'matched' from queueActive (`const queueActive = !['idle','matched'].includes(queue.state.status)`) or add a brief 'Matched!' visual state to the overlay.

findings.issue: CATEGORY_SLUG = 'tech' is hardcoded in both the hook and the ChallengeCard callback. A shared constant would prevent divergence.
findings.fix: Extract to a shared constant in a lib file, or pass categorySlug as a parameter to the hook.

learnings.insight: The mobile CSS has no global button:focus-visible fallback (unlike globals.css in the web app). Every interactive element in the mobile app needs explicit focus-visible:ring-* Tailwind classes. ModeCard and SearchingOverlay buttons are missing them.
learnings.action: Add focus-visible classes to ModeCard and all SearchingOverlay buttons to match the pattern used by Play hero, ProfileScreen toggles, and BottomNav.

learnings.insight: The join() function lacks the double-tap guard that startChallenge has (challengeBusy check). On rapid double-tap, two POSTs fire before the overlay renders to block further taps.
learnings.action: Add a status or ref guard at the top of join() to prevent concurrent calls, matching the challengeBusy pattern.

learnings.insight: Reviewed 2 changed files (useMatchmakingQueue.ts: 213 lines new, HomeScreen.tsx: 510 lines total). 0 critical, 2 warning, 3 info findings.
